---
title: "sandbox"
---

```{r}

library(gt)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Create dummy data
data <- data.frame(
  Col1 = c("A", "B", "C", "A", " "),
  Col2 = c("C", "A", " ", "B", "A"),
  Col3 = c("B", " ", "A", "C", "B")
)

# 2. Create the table
data %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(
    columns = everything(), # Apply to all columns
    fn = function(x) {
      # Return "yellow" if value is "A", otherwise no color (NA)
      ifelse(x == "A", "yellow", "white")
    }
  )

```


```{r}
# 1. Initialize the gt object
my_table <- data %>% 
  gt()

# 2. Loop through every column name to apply the style dynamically
for(col in names(data)) {
  my_table <- my_table %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "yellow"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = all_of(col),
        # The logic: Apply if the cell in this specific column equals "A"
        rows = .data[[col]] == "A" 
      )
    ) %>%
  tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "lightblue"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = all_of(col),
        # The logic: Apply if the cell in this specific column equals "B"
        rows = .data[[col]] == "B" 
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(color = "lightblue"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = all_of(col),
        # The logic: Apply if the cell in this specific column equals "B"
        rows = .data[[col]] == "B" 
      )
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_fill(color = "lightgreen"),
      locations = cells_body(
        columns = all_of(col),
        # The logic: Apply if the cell in this specific column equals "C"
        rows = .data[[col]] == "C" 
      )
    )
}

my_table
```


```{r}
library(gt)
# 1. Create dummy data
data <- data.frame(
  Col1 = c("E", "2", "5", "1", " "),
  Col2 = c("A", "1", "8", "4", "1"),
  Col3 = c("T", " ", "3", "6", "2")
)

# 2. Generate 8 colors (for values 0 through 7)
my_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("white", "honeydew4"))(8)

# 3. Create the table
my_table <- data %>%
  gt() %>%
  data_color(
    columns = everything(),
    # Define a custom function to map values to colors
    fn = function(x) {
      # Define your lookup list
      colors <- c("1" = my_colors[2], 
                  "2" = my_colors[3], 
                  "3" = my_colors[4], 
                  "4" = my_colors[5],
                  "5" = my_colors[6],
                  "6" = my_colors[7],
                  "7" = my_colors[8], 
                  "8" = "red", 
                  " " = my_colors[1])
      
      # Create the vector of mapped colors
      # We ensure x is character to prevent errors if the column is a Factor
      result_colors <- colors[as.character(x)] 
      
      # Find any NAs (values not in the list) and set them to white
      result_colors[is.na(result_colors)] <- "white"
      
      return(result_colors)
    }
  )

my_table
```

```{r}

## Create a function for the color overlay
bb_color_map <- function(
  max_val = 7,
  low = "white",
  high = "honeydew4",
  overflow = "white",
  blanks = c("", " ", NA)
) {
  ## Palette has (max_val + 1) steps: 0..max_val
  pal <- colorRampPalette(c(low, high))(max_val + 1)

  ## Map 0..max_val
  m <- setNames(pal, as.character(0:max_val))

  ## Add blank variants -> low color
  for (b in blanks) {
    if (is.na(b)) next
    m[[b]] <- pal[1]
  }

  list(map = m, pal = pal, max_val = max_val, overflow = overflow)
}

## Build the mapping
cm <- bb_color_map(max_val = 7, 
                   low = "white", 
                   high = "honeydew4", 
                   overflow = "white")

## Apply color using a lookup function
gt_tbl_colored <- gt_tbl %>%
  gt::data_color(
    columns = gt::everything(),  ## or restrict to site columns; see note below
    fn = function(x) {
      ## Work in character space
      x_chr <- as.character(x)
      x_chr[is.na(x_chr)] <- "0"   ## treat NA as 0 (blank)

      ## Flag out-of-range numeric values
      suppressWarnings(x_num <- as.numeric(x_chr))
      over <- !is.na(x_num) & (x_num < 0 | x_num > cm$max_val)

      ## Default: map using known keys; unknown values go to white
      out <- cm$map[x_chr]
      out[is.na(out)] <- cm$map[["0"]]

      ## Overflow highlight
      out[over] <- cm$overflow

      out
    }
  )

gt_tbl_colored

  
  

```
